newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian shrs edge up by close, unfazed by strike.
newsitem.headline: Colombian shrs edge up by close, unfazed by strike.

text.p: Colombian stocks were driven marginally higher by demand for brewing and cement shares, unfazed by a nationwide strike of government workers.
Bogota's IBB index edged up 0.05 percent to 1,021.56 in volume of 1.7 billion pesos, while Medellin's IBOMED general price index gained 0.6 percent to close at 15,885.89 in 1.8 billion peso trade.

"The market was being driven by foreign funds. The strike had little effect because shares bought today will only be paid for Friday and the real impact of the work stoppage is marginal," said one Bogota broker.
"No real key sector was paralyzed, and despite a go-slow in part of the banking sector, investors believe things will be back to normal tomorrow," he added.

Foreign fund demand drove up brewing giant Bavaria 2.04 percent to 6,500 in Bogota, and in Medellin it rose 3.2 percent to 6,580. Cement manufacturer Cemento Argos, one of the flagship companies of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate, rose 1.63 percent to 7,013 in Bogota and gained 1.9 percent in Medellin to 7,031.
"The perception by foreign funds is that the strike lacked grassroots support, and they believe it will become weaker as it fails to affect economic activities," a Medellin-based broker said.

Union leaders, however, described support for the strike as "total" and claimed success in severely disrupting the nation's airports, oil and coffee industries, telecommunications, schools and all but emergency health care.
The main losers of the day were banks. Banco de Bogota dropped 1.58 percent to 6,200, while Banco Ganadero ordinary shares fell back 0.63 percent to 316.
"When foreign funds focus on one or two specific stocks, then all the others tend to fall," another Medellin broker said.

Banco de Colombia remained unchanged in both markets. The bank is currently negotiating a deal to sell a stake of between 26 percent and 35 percent to Spain's Banco Central Hispano and as a result recently upped its debt provision -- which led to a drop in 1996 profits.
